card: This PR modifies BlockAssembler to use strict greater-than checks when testing whether a mempool chunk exceeds block weight or sigops limits. Currently, checks use greater-than-or-equal, preventing chunks from filling the template to its exact maximum capacity despite BIP 141 consensus limits permitting equality. The change allows exact-fit transactions to be included, resolving an off-by-one underfill issue in block template creation.
changed_since_previous: Added release notes and documentation updates clarifying that miners must reserve adequate weight and sigop budgets for coinbase construction, and updated unit tests.
evidence: PR description notes that BIP 141 defines both consensus limits using ≤, making exact equality valid.
PR description cites an unaddressed 2016 review comment on PR #7600 pointing out the same inclusive-limit issue.
Addresses part of issue #35596 (`BlockAssembler underfill blocks and mixes reserve weights`).
problem: `BlockAssembler` rejects mempool chunks that would bring total block weight to `block_max_weight` or total sigops to `MAX_BLOCK_SIGOPS_COST` exactly, even though BIP 141 defines both consensus limits inclusively (≤). This leaves valid block capacity unused and drops fee-paying transactions that fit exact limits.

risk.why: A boundary error in miner block limit calculations could cause miners to produce invalid blocks exceeding consensus limits that get rejected by the network.

summary: Switches `BlockAssembler::TestChunkBlockLimits` comparisons from `>=` to `>` for block weight and sigop costs. This allows block templates to include transactions that bring accounted weight or sigops exactly to their configured maximum limits.
